makaleler.baslik: Improving Quality Through the Emergency General Surgery Verification Program.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Emergency General Surgery Doğrulama Programı ile Kalite İyileştirme
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 55 hastanede 21858 hastanın değerlendirildiği bu kohort çalışmasında, Acil Cerrahi doğrulama programı hastanede kalış süresinde (-1,31 gün; %95 CI, -1,95 ile -0,67), AKI oranında (%-1,23; %95 CI, -2,00 ile -0,46) ve 30 günlük mortalitede (%-1,63; %95 CI, -2,55 ile -0,71) anlamlı düşüşlerle ilişkilendirilmiştir.
makaleler.ozet:
IMPORTANCE: The Emergency General Surgery Verification Program was designed and launched in 2023 by the American College of Surgeons to standardize and improve EGS care through 43 standards that support hospital structure, care processes, and outcome surveillance.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between EGS verification and hospital length of stay (LOS), acute kidney injury (AKI), and 30-day mortality and to assess whether changes in care processes contribute to effects.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This quasi-experimental difference-in-differences cohort study with staggered adoption used data from the ACS National Surgical Quality Improvement Program EGS Targeted Dataset. Patients with operatively managed EGS diagnoses from July 1, 2023, through December 31, 2024, at 50 control and 5 verified hospitals were evaluated. Data were analyzed from July 2025 through February 2026.
EXPOSURE: Hospital EGS verification status.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes were mean LOS, 30-day mortality rate, and AKI rate. These were calculated adjusted and unadjusted. Average treatment effects on the treated were estimated with hospital-clustered bootstrap standard errors.
RESULTS: The final cohort included 21 858 patients at 55 hospitals. Median (IQR) patient age was 53.2 (36.5-68.5) years, and 12 366 patients (56.6%) were female. Prior to verification, verified hospitals treated higher-acuity patients and had higher predicted mortality and AKI rates. Verification was associated with absolute reductions in LOS (-1.31 days; 95% CI, -1.95 to -0.67), AKI (-1.23 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.00 to -0.46), and mortality (-1.63 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.55 to -0.71), corresponding to relative reductions of 19.7%, 29.0%, and 28.8%, respectively. These results held after risk adjustment and Bonferroni correction. Verification was also associated with improved care processes, including increased admission to surgical services (74.8% to 85.7%; P < .001), decreased failure of nonoperative management (25.5% to 19.0%; P < .001), and shorter time to operation (-10.7 hours; P < .001). All processes were independently associated with improvements in all 3 primary outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study, early adoption of ACS EGS verification was associated with clinically meaningful reductions in LOS, AKI, and 30-day mortality among participating hospitals. These findings demonstrate the EGS verification likely drives systems-level improvements in emergency surgical care, which may be partially explained by improvements in performance on hospital process measures.

makaleler.baslik: Acute cholecystitis during pregnancy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Gebelikte Akut Kolesistit: Sistematik Derleme ve Meta-Analiz
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Gebelerde akut kolesistitin yönetimi incelendi. 90 çalışmanın dahil edildiği meta-analizde, cerrahi ve cerrahi dışı takip arasında sezaryen, erken doğum veya komplikasyonlar açısından fark bulunmazken; cerrahi grupta venöz tromboembolizm riski daha düşük saptandı (RR 0,55; %95 CI 0,37-0,82).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Acute cholecystitis is an uncommon non-obstetric surgical emergency in pregnancy, yet guidance on management remains inconsistent. This systematic review and meta-analysis examined presentation, diagnostics, management, and outcomes of pregnant patients diagnosed with acute cholecystitis.
METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched from inception to February 2024 (PROSPERO CRD42022350290). Eligible studies reported acute cholecystitis in pregnancy with individual patient data or extractable cohort data. Risk of bias was assessed in duplicates. Descriptive statistics summarised individual data, and random-effects meta-analysis generated pooled risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence interval (CI).
RESULTS: Ninety studies (1964-2023) were included: 48 case reports/series (n = 118), 19 descriptive cohorts (n = 5,702), 19 cohorts comparing operative versus non-operative care (n = 91,955), and 4 cohorts comparing laparoscopic versus open surgery (n = 62,620). Among cases with symptom data (n = 75), right-upper-quadrant pain (40%), vomiting (33%), nausea (29%), and fever (17%) predominated. Imaging (n = 92) most often showed gallstones (42%) and ultrasonographic cholecystitis or wall thickening (21%). Of the cases with management data (n = 93), surgery was performed in 81 (laparoscopic 71/81; percutaneous drainage 10/81; open 1/81);12 were managed non-operatively. Of 83 with outcomes, 84% had uncomplicated courses. Meta-analysis found no significant differences between operative and non-operative care for caesarean delivery, preterm birth, postpartum haemorrhage, or composite complications, but venous thromboembolism risk was lower with surgery (RR 0.55, 95% CI 0.37-0.82), although this outcome was reported by only two studies.
CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound-based diagnosis and laparoscopic cholecystectomy appear safe across all trimesters of pregnancy, with obstetric outcomes comparable to non-operative management. Operative management was associated with a lower observed risk of venous thromboembolism, although this finding was based on limited evidence. Further prospective studies are needed to optimise patient selection and surgical timing.

makaleler.baslik: Compliance with French Military Health Service guidelines for prehospital transfusion of blood products during forward aeromedical evacuations in Sahel (2015 to 2023).
makaleler.baslik_tr: Fransız Askeri Sağlık Servisi Prehospital Transfüzyon Kılavuz Uyumu
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Sahel bölgesinde 2015 ile 2023 yılları arasında travma nedeniyle tahliye edilen 206 hastanın incelendiği retrospektif çalışmada, transfüzyon kriterlerini karşılamanın transfüzyon gereksinimi ile ilişkili olduğu saptanmıştır (RR 3,20; %95 CI [2,29-4,47]; p=10^-7). Transfüze edilen hastaların %65'i belirlenen kriterleri karşılamamıştır.
makaleler.ozet:
INTRODUCTION: The forward transfusion guideline of the French Health Service (FHS) provides guidance for prehospital blood product (BP) transfusion in casualties' evacuations from overseas operations (OO). In Sahel, aeromedical evacuation (AE) teams are provided with lyophilized plasma, packed red blood cells (PRBC), and cold-stored low-titer group O whole blood (CS-LTOWB). The main objective was to evaluate compliance with guidelines for prehospital transfusion of severely injured trauma casualties during forward AE in OO. Secondary objectives were to identify clinical and paraclinical criteria, beyond current guidelines, associated with transfusion, and to describe the factors influencing transfusion rates.
METHODS: A multicenter retrospective observational study was conducted on forward AE missions in the western Sahelian theater between January 2015 and July 2023. Two hundred and six patients evacuated for traumatic injuries, classified as category Alpha or Bravo, were included.
RESULTS: Sixty-four wounded received prehospital transfusion of eighty-nine BP units. Meeting transfusion criteria was associated with the requirement for transfusion (p = 10-7, relative risk (RR): 3.20 with 95% confidence interval (95% CI) [2.29-4.47]). Sixty-five percent of transfused patients did not meet the established transfusion criteria. Isolated heart rate above 110 bpm, modification of complexion, Shock Index above 1, altered mental status, penetrating trauma, pelvic trauma and effusion at Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma (FAST) ultrasound were more frequent within transfused patients. Median transfusion rate was about 25 mL/min [16-50].
CONCLUSION: A prospective evaluation of our findings is needed before proposing a revision to the current FHS guideline, including the addition of exclusion criteria.

makaleler.baslik: Timing matters: Delayed surgery increases mortality for blunt hollow viscus injury.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Geciken Cerrahi Künt İçi Boşluklu Organ Yaralanmasında Mortaliteyi Artırır
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Künt karın travmalı 33.728 hastanın incelendiği çalışmada, 8 saatten geç yapılan bağırsak rezeksiyonu/onarımı (DBR) değerlendirildi. 16.010 hastaya (%47,5) DBR uygulandı ve bu grubun artmış mortalite riski ile ilişkili olduğu görüldü (%13,0'e karşı %8,5; OR 1,21; %95 CI 1,12-1,30; p<0,001).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Immediate surgical exploration is recommended for suspected hollow viscus injury (HVI) following blunt trauma. However, diagnostic uncertainty can lead to delayed operative management. We aimed to evaluate if delayed bowel resection/repair (DBR), defined as ≥8 hours after emergency department arrival, was independently associated with increased mortality in blunt trauma patients. We also sought to identify risk factors associated with DBR.
METHODS: The Trauma Quality Improvement Program database (2017-2024) was queried for admitted adults with blunt abdominal trauma (abdomen abbreviated injury scale grade ≥2) who underwent bowel resection/repair. Patients who were transferred from another facility or died within 8 hours were excluded. Patients undergoing early bowel resection <8 hours (EBR) were compared with patients undergoing DBR (≥8 h). Multivariable logistic regression evaluated the association between DBR and mortality, controlling for age, severe head and thoracic injury, intubation within 1 hour of arrival, injury to the small bowel, colon, or rectum, and blood transfusion within 4 hours.
RESULTS: Of 33,728 patients undergoing bowel resection/repair, 16,010 (47.5%) underwent DBR. The DBR cohort had lower rates of small bowel (49.6% vs. 53.9%, p<0.001) and colon (46.7% vs. 49.7%, p<0.001) injuries, but similar rates of rectal injury (4.4% vs. 4.1%, p=0.166). Injuries to the liver (26.8% vs. 20.8%), spleen (28.2% vs. 23.4%), and kidney (12.9% vs. 9.0%) were more frequent in the DBR cohort (all p<0.001). DBR patients had an increased associated risk of mortality (13.0% vs. 8.5%, OR 1.21, 95% CI: 1.12-1.30, p<0.001). Small bowel injury was the only independent factor with decreased associated risk of DBR (OR 0.93, CI: 0.89-0.97, p=0.001).
CONCLUSION: Delayed operative management for blunt HVI occurs more often in patients with solid organ injuries and is independently associated with increased mortality. These findings highlight the importance of early detection and timely surgical management of HVI.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Therapeutic/Care Management, Level IV.

makaleler.baslik: A Randomized Trial Comparing Two Balanced Crystalloids in Patients Undergoing Emergency Exploratory Laparotomy for Blunt Abdominal Trauma Under General Anesthesia.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Künt Abdominal Travmada Acil Laparotomi İçin İki Kristaloidin Karşılaştırılması
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Künt abdominal travma nedeniyle acil eksploratuar laparotomi yapılan 60 yetişkin hastada yapılan prospektif, randomize, çift kör çalışmada, asetat bazlı solüsyonun laktat bazlı solüsyona kıyasla postoperatif pH stabilitesini korumada ve laktat yükünden kaçınmada daha avantajlı olduğu gösterilmiştir.
makaleler.ozet:
INTRODUCTION: Intravenous crystalloids are central to perioperative resuscitation of patients with blunt abdominal trauma, in whom haemorrhage and hypoperfusion produce metabolic acidosis and hyperlactatemia. Balanced crystalloids are preferred over 0.9% saline, but it is unclear whether the choice of buffer anion-lactate versus acetate-influences perioperative acid-base and electrolyte status. We compared a lactated balanced crystalloid with an acetated balanced crystalloid in this setting.
METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, double-blind study conducted at a level-1 trauma centre, sixty adults (18-50 years) undergoing exploratory laparotomy lasting more than one hour for blunt abdominal trauma were allocated to receive a lactated balanced crystalloid (Group R, n = 30) or an acetated balanced crystalloid (Group S, n = 30). Arterial blood gas, base excess, lactate and serum electrolytes were recorded at baseline (preoperative) and after surgery (postoperative). Intergroup and intragroup comparisons were performed using Student's t-test, Mann-Whitney U test, and Chi-square or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate; p < 0.05 was considered significant.
RESULTS: Demographic profiles and duration of surgery were comparable between groups. Group R showed a significant postoperative fall in pH (p = 0.041), whereas pH remained stable in Group S; the postoperative intergroup difference favoured the acetated solution (p = 0.012). Base excess improved significantly within both groups (Group R p = 0.019; Group S p = 0.031), with no significant intergroup difference. Lactate fell significantly in Group S (p = 0.027) but not in Group R, and the postoperative intergroup comparison favoured the acetated solution (p = 0.049). Bicarbonate and all measured electrolytes (Na⁺, K⁺, Cl⁻, Ca²⁺) remained stable, with no significant intra- or intergroup differences.
CONCLUSION: The acetated solution provided marginally better pH stability and avoided the exogenous lactate load associated with the lactated solution.

turk.baslik: Traumatic diaphragmatic injuries from the perspective of thoracic and general surgery: analysis of patient management using the Injury Severity Score (ISS) and Modified Shock Index (MSI).
turk.baslik_tr: Travmatik Diyafragma Yaralanmaları: Göğüs ve Genel Cerrahi Perspektifi
turk.kisa_ozet: Cerrahi tedavi uygulanan 41 travmatik diyafragma yaralanmalı hastanın incelendiği çalışmada, %37,5 genel komplikasyon oranı ve en sık atelektazi (%26,7) görüldü. Genel Cerrahi tarafından ameliyat edilen hastalarda ISS skorları Göğüs Cerrahisine göre anlamlı derecede yüksek saptandı.
turk.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Traumatic diaphragmatic injury (TDI) is a rare but severe clinical condition associated with high mortality following blunt or penetrating thoracoabdominal trauma. Due to concomitant injuries, the diagnosis of traumatic diaphragmatic injury remains challenging and may be easily overlooked. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnosis and surgical management of traumatic diaphragmatic injuries through a retrospective analysis conducted at a single center between 2016 and 2024.
METHODS: Data from 41 patients who underwent surgical treatment for TDI between 2016 and 2024 were analyzed. Patients were classified into three groups according to the diagnostic process: those diagnosed intraoperatively without prior imaging (Group 1), those who underwent imaging but were diagnosed intraoperatively (Group 2), and those diagnosed preoperatively by computed tomography (CT) (Group 3). Demographic characteristics, mechanisms of injury, surgical approaches, postoperative complications, and prognostic scores, including the Injury Severity Score (ISS) and Modified Shock Index (MSI), were evaluated.
RESULTS: Most patients were male (97.6%), and the left hemidiaphragm was the most frequently injured side (63.4%). Penetrating trauma (68.2%) was more common than blunt trauma, with gunshot wounds (34.1%) and stab wounds (34.1%) representing the most common mechanisms of injury. Laparotomy was the most frequently performed surgical approach (41.5%), and primary repair was achieved in 92.5% of patients. The overall postoperative complication rate was 37.5%, with atelectasis being the most common complication (26.7%). ISS scores were significantly higher in patients diagnosed intraoperatively than in those diagnosed preoperatively by imaging (p<0.001). Patients who underwent surgery within the first two hours after admission had higher ISS scores than those who underwent delayed surgery (p<0.001). ISS scores were significantly higher among patients operated on by the General Surgery department than among those treated by the Thoracic Surgery department. In contrast, MSI scores were lower in Thoracic Surgery patients who underwent emergency surgery for hemothorax than in General Surgery patients.
CONCLUSION: TDI remains a diagnostically challenging condition, and early surgical intervention is crucial for reducing mortality. Despite advances in imaging techniques, some cases continue to be overlooked because of concomitant injuries. Therefore, a high index of clinical suspicion and close patient monitoring are essential for timely diagnosis. Furthermore, differences in ISS and MSI scores between patients managed by different surgical specialties may reflect variations in trauma severity, surgical decision-making, and timing of intervention.

tez.baslik: Akut apandisit tanılı hastaların preoperatif serum alfa defensin 5 düzeylerinin ameliyat sonuçlarına göre karşılaştırılması
tez.baslik_tr: Akut Apandisitte Preoperatif Serum Alfa Defensin 5 Düzeylerinin Karşılaştırılması
tez.kisa_ozet: 180 hastanın dahil olduğu prospektif çalışmada, alfa defensin-5 düzeyinin negatif gruba kıyasla akut ve perfore gruplarda anlamlı olarak arttığı saptandı (p1=0,002; p2<0,001). Alfa defensin-5 düzeyi akut apandisit için bağımsız ve güçlü bir etken olarak bulundu (β=0,903; %95 CI 0,506-1,30; p<0,001).
tez.ozet: Amaç: Bu çalışmada akut apandisit tanısıyla operasyon planlanan hastalardan operasyon öncesi alınan serum alfa defensin-5 değerlerinin karşılaştırılması ve akut apandisit ile ilişkisinin değerlendirilmesi amaçlandı. Gereç ve yöntem: Çalışmamıza Nisan 2025 – Nisan 2026 tarihleri arasında hastanemizin Genel Cerrahi Kliniği'ne başvuran ve akut apandisit ön tanısıyla operasyon kararı verilen 180 hasta prospektif olarak dahil edildi. Hastalardan serum alfa defensin 5 değerleri için kan alındı. Hastaların yaşı, cinsiyeti, beden kitle indeksi (BKI), bilgisayarlı tomografideki (BT) apendiks çapları, kanda lökosit ve C-reaktif protein (CRP) değerleri ve apandisit semptomlarının varlığı kaydedildi. Değişken parametreler gruplara göre karşılaştırıldı. Bulgular: Çalışmaya dahil edilen hastaların yaş ortalaması 31,9 ± 8,7, BKI ortalaması 26,4 ± 5,5 olarak bulundu. Alfa defensin-5 düzeyinin negatif gruba kıyasla hem akut (13,08 ± 6,33; p1=0,002) hem de perfore (14,80 ± 7,95;p2<0,001) gruplarda anlamlı olarak artmış olduğu ancak akut ve perfore gruplar arasında anlamlı fark olmadığı saptandı (p3=0,368). Regresyon analizlerinde boy, kilo, beden kitle indeksi, erkek cinsiyet ve lökositoz akut apandisit gelişiminde anlamlı olarak bulundu. Perfore apandisitle negatif grup karşılaştırıldığında BT'de apendiks çapı, alfa defensin-5 düzeyi, yaş, boy, kilo, bki, C-reaktif protein, lökosit sayısı ve rebound anlamlı değişkenler olarak bulundu. Akut apandisit ile negatif grup karşılaştırıldığında, alfa defensin-5 düzeyi (β=0,903; %95 CI 0,506–1,30; p<0,001)bağımsız ve güçlü bir etken olarak saptandı. Sonuç: Bu çalışma ile preoperatif serum alfa defensin 5 değerlerinde negatif apendektomi grubu ile akut apandisit tanısı doğrulanan hastalar arasında anlamlı fark olduğu tespit edildi. Ancak akut apandisit ile perfore apandisit olan hastalar arasında anlamlı fark olmadığı tespit edildi. Çalışmamızın desteklenmesi ve daha net sonuçlara ulaşılabilmesi için bu konuyla ilgili daha kapsamlı ve multidisipliner prospektif çalışmalara gerek olduğunu düşünmekteyiz. Anahtar Kelimeler: Akut apandisit, Perfore apandisit, Prediktif değer, Alfa defensin 5, Negatif apendektomi

makaleler.baslik: Efficacy and Safety of Prophylactic Defect Closure After Colorectal ESD: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis with GRADE Certainty Assessment.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Kolorektal ESD Sonrası Profilaktik Defekt Kapatma
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 5.830 prosedürü içeren 16 çalışmanın sistematik derleme ve meta-analizinde, kolorektal ESD sonrası profilaktik defekt kapatmanın gecikmiş kanama riskini azalttığı gösterildi (RR 0,42; %95 CI, 0,28-0,62; pooled oranlar %2,4'e karşı %6,9). Gecikmiş perforasyon veya hastane kalış süresinde fark görülmedi.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Colorectal endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) leaves a large mucosal defect that predisposes patients to delayed adverse events, chiefly delayed bleeding. Prophylactic closure of the defect has been proposed to improve safety, but its overall efficacy remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis provides an updated synthesis of the safety and efficacy of prophylactic mucosal defect closure after colorectal ESD.
METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched from inception to June 2026, without language restrictions, for randomized controlled trials and comparative observational studies comparing prophylactic closure with no closure after colorectal ESD. The primary outcome was delayed bleeding; secondary outcomes were delayed perforation, post-ESD coagulation syndrome (PECS), and length of hospital stay. Pooled RRs and mean differences with 95% CIs were calculated using random-effects models, and the certainty of evidence was assessed with GRADE.
RESULTS: Sixteen studies comprising 5,830 procedures were included. Prophylactic closure was associated with a lower risk of delayed bleeding (RR 0.42; 95% CI, 0.28 to 0.62; I² = 63.9%), with pooled delayed bleeding rates of 2.4% with closure and 6.9% without closure. No difference was observed for delayed perforation (RR 0.89; 95% CI, 0.37 to 2.17), PECS (RR 1.12; 95% CI, 0.50 to 2.49), or length of hospital stay (mean difference 0.16 days; 95% CI, -0.61 to 0.93). Small-study effects were detected for delayed bleeding, and the certainty of evidence ranged from low to very low.
CONCLUSIONS: Prophylactic closure after colorectal ESD reduced delayed bleeding. No effect on delayed perforation, PECS, or length of hospital stay was shown, although these estimates were imprecise. Closure may be best reserved for patients at high risk of bleeding.
makaleler.dergi_tam: Journal of gastrointestinal surgery : official journal of the Society for Surgery of the Alimentary Tract

makaleler.baslik: Efficacy of Endoscopic Hand Suturing for Prevention of Adverse Events After Gastric Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection: A Multicenter Propensity Score-Matched Study.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Gastrik ESD Sonrası Endoskopik El Dikişi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Üç merkezli, proporsiyon skor eşleşmeli retrospektif çalışmada, gastrik ESD sonrası endoskopik el dikişi (EHS) grubunda advers olaylar %1,6 ile kontrol grubundaki %8,9'a kıyasla anlamlı derecede düşük bulundu (P < 0,01). Özellikle gecikmiş kanama %1,6'ya karşı %8,4 oranında azaldı (P < 0,01). Dikiş açılma oranı %27 olmasına rağmen kanama riskini artırmadı.
makaleler.ozet: Background and study aims Post-endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) mucosal defects are associated with risks of delayed bleeding and perforation. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of endoscopic hand suturing (EHS) for gastric ESD ulcers and to identify factors influencing its success and durability. Patients and methods We conducted a multicenter retrospective study using propensity score matching (1:3 ratio) at three institutions between 2020 and 2024. The EHS group (n=123) was compared with a non-EHS control group comprising both historical and contemporaneous controls (n=369). The primary endpoint was the overall incidence of post-ESD adverse events. Secondary outcomes included delayed bleeding, delayed perforation, technical success, suturing time, and dehiscence rates. Results Post-ESD adverse events were significantly lower in the EHS group compared to the non-EHS group (1.6% vs. 8.9%, P < 0.01). Specifically, delayed bleeding was markedly reduced (1.6% vs. 8.4%, P < 0.01). Exploratory analysis using the BEST-J classification showed numerically larger absolute risk reductions in the high-risk and very high-risk categories (21.5% and 40.0%, respectively). Complete closure was achieved in 124 of 131 EHS procedures (94.7%), with a median suturing time of 52.5 minutes. Although the dehiscence rate on postoperative day 5 was 27%, it did not increase the risk of delayed bleeding. Learning curve analysis showed that complete closure rates approached 100% after approximately 25 cases. Conclusions EHS was safely performed and was associated with fewer adverse events after gastric ESD. Procedural efficiency and success improved significantly with operator experience.

makaleler.baslik: High-flow versus standard nasal cannula oxygenation during prone-position ERCP under nurse-administered propofol sedation: a randomized controlled trial.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Pron Pozisyonda ERCP Sırasında Yüksek Akışlı Nazal Kanül
makaleler.kisa_ozet: İki merkezli, prospektif RCT'de, propofol sedasyonu altında pron pozisyonda ERCP yapılan 300 hastada yüksek akışlı nazal kanül (HFNC) standart nazal kanüle (SNC) kıyasla hipoksemiyi azalttı (%1,3'e karşı %14,0; RR 0,10, %95 CI 0,02-0,36; P < 0,001). HFNC grubunda geçici hipotansiyon daha sık görüldü (%16,7'ye karşı %8,0; P = 0,02).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Hypoxemia affects up to 23% of patients undergoing ERCP under nurse-administered propofol sedation (NAPS) with a standard nasal cannula (SNC). High-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) provides heated, humidified oxygen at high gas flow with more controlled inspired oxygen delivery than conventional low-flow oxygen and may reduce hypoxemic events during sedation. We compared HFNC with SNC during ERCP under NAPS.
METHODS: In this two-center, prospective, randomized trial, 300 adults undergoing ERCP between October 2025 and June 2026 were allocated 1:1 to HFNC (flow 50 L/min; FiO2 0.50) or SNC (5 L/min). All procedures were performed in the prone position under propofol-based NAPS. The primary outcome was hypoxemia (SpO2 < 92% for > 10 s). Secondary outcomes included airway interventions and cardiovascular events.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics, procedural factors, and sedation dosages were comparable. Hypoxemia occurred in 2 of 150 patients (1.3%) with HFNC versus 21 of 150 (14.0%) with SNC (RR 0.10, 95% CI 0.02-0.36; P < 0.001). Jaw-thrust maneuvers (1.3 vs. 12.0%; P < 0.001) and nasopharyngeal airway insertion (0 vs. 9.3%; P < 0.001) were also less frequent with HFNC. No patient required emergency intubation. Hypotension was more frequent with HFNC (16.7 vs. 8.0%; P = 0.02), but no episode required vasopressors or procedure termination. In post hoc analyses, HFNC reduced hypoxemic events in both BMI subgroups; however, the treatment-by-BMI interaction was not significant (P for interaction = 0.65).
CONCLUSIONS: HFNC oxygenation strategy reduced hypoxemic events and rescue airway interventions during ERCP under NAPS, although transient hypotension occurred more frequently. No significant treatment-by-BMI interaction was observed.
TRIAL REGISTRY: Thai Clinical Trials Registry, TCTR20250901001.

makaleler.baslik: Pharmacological and procedural strategies to prevent post-ERCP pancreatitis: an umbrella review of meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Post-ERCP Pankreatit Önlemede Farmakolojik ve Teknik Stratejiler
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 137391 katılımcıyı içeren 47 meta-analizin incelendiği umbrella review çalışmasında, post-ERCP pankreatit (PEP) önlemede indometazin (OR 0,52; %95 CI 0,39-0,71), epinefrin (RR 0,34; %95 CI 0,18-0,62) ve pankreatik stent yerleştirme (RR 0,37; %95 CI 0,27-0,51) etkili bulunmuştur.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Post-endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) pancreatitis (PEP) is the most common complication following ERCP, and its prevention remains a major concern for biliopancreatic endoscopists. This umbrella review aims to assess existing meta-analytic evidence on the effectiveness of pharmacological interventions (PIs) and procedural technical modifications (PTMs) in reducing the incidence and severity of PEP.
METHODS: We searched multiple databases to identify meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that assessed the impacts of PIs or PTMs on the incidence and severity of PEP, from database inception to September 24, 2024. Evidence credibility was classified based on pre-specified criteria as: convincing (Class I), highly suggestive (Class II), suggestive (Class III), weak (Class IV), or non-significant evidence. Furthermore, the GRADE approach was employed to assess the quality of the evidence, categorizing it into four levels: high, moderate, low, and very low.
RESULTS: A review of 47 meta-analyses (137,391 participants; 25 on PIs, 22 on PTMs) identified five PIs with suggestive evidence for PEP prevention: indomethacin (odds ratio [OR] 0.52, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.39-0.71), epinephrine (risk ratio [RR] 0.34, 95% CI 0.18-0.62), nafamostat mesylate (RR 0.50, 0.38-0.66), NSAIDs (RR 0.65, 0.52-0.81), and aggressive hydration (OR 0.40, 0.26-0.63). For PTMs, one intervention was classified as highly suggestive evidence: pancreatic stent placement (RR 0.37, 0.27-0.51), while guidewire-assisted cannulation was suggestive (RR 0.51, 0.36-0.72). For high-risk patients, both indomethacin (RR 0.46, 0.32-0.65) and pancreatic stent placement (RR 0.41, 0.30-0.56) were suggestive. No interventions exceeded Class III evidence for preventing moderate to severe PEP.
CONCLUSIONS: Pancreatic stent placement and NSAIDs, such as indomethacin, have been confirmed as effective measures for PEP prevention in both unselected and high-risk patients.

makaleler.baslik: Anorectal function after transanal natural orifice specimen extraction for colorectal cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Kolorektal Kanser İçin Transanal NOSE Sonrası Anorektal Fonksiyon
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 1.362 hastayı içeren 7 retrospektif kohort çalışmasının meta-analizinde, transanal NOSE ile transabdominal ekstraksiyon (TASE) karşılaştırıldı. Yaklaşık 6. ayda Wexner skorları transanal NOSE sonrasında sayısal olarak biraz daha yüksek bulundu ancak bu fark istatistiksel olarak anlamlı değildi (MD 0,17, %95 CI -0,01 ila 0,35; p = 0,07).
makaleler.ozet:
PURPOSE: Natural orifice specimen extraction (NOSE) eliminates the abdominal extraction incision after minimally invasive (MIS) colorectal resection and offers favourable short-term recovery, but transanal extraction raises concerns regarding sphincter stretch and anorectal dysfunction. This review evaluated anorectal functional outcomes after transanal NOSE compared with transabdominal specimen extraction (TASE) in MIS colorectal cancer surgery.
METHODS: MEDLINE and EMBASE were searched from inception to August 2024 for comparative studies reporting postoperative anorectal or pelvic floor functional outcomes following transanal NOSE versus TASE. The primary outcome was anorectal continence at the postoperative interval closest to 6 months.
RESULTS: Ten retrospective cohort studies were included, of which seven (1362 patients) contributed quantitative data for meta-analysis. Three studies contributed to the pooled Wexner incontinence score analysis and four to the pooled Pelvic Floor Distress Inventory short form (PFDI-20) analysis. At the interval closest to 6 months, Wexner scores were numerically higher after transanal NOSE than TASE, but the difference was small and non-significant (MD 0.17, 95% CI - 0.01 to 0.35; p = 0.07). PFDI-20 scores did not differ between groups (MD - 0.02, 95% CI - 0.21 to 0.18; p = 0.86). Both estimates were robust in leave-one-out and overlap-adjusted analyses excluding potentially overlapping Harbin Medical University cohorts. Early differences appeared to diminish over time, with no clear separation beyond 12 months.
CONCLUSION: Transanal NOSE was associated with a small, non-significant trend toward higher early Wexner scores after MIS colorectal cancer surgery, while broader pelvic floor symptom burden appeared comparable to TASE. The difference was of uncertain clinical significance, was robust to sensitivity analyses, and longer-term data suggested no persistent functional disadvantage.

tez.baslik: Akalazya hastalarında laparoskopik Heller miyotomi sonrası cerrahi sonuçlar ve yaşam kalitesini etkileyen faktörler
tez.baslik_tr: Laparoskopik Heller Miyotomi Sonrası Cerrahi Sonuçlar
tez.kisa_ozet: Tip II akalazya nedeniyle laparoskopik Heller miyotomi ve Dor fundoplikasyonu uygulanan 56 hastanın incelendiği çalışmada, intraoperatif komplikasyon oranı %3,6, nüks oranı %12,5 bulunmuştur. Toplam Eckardt skoru preoperatif 7,5'ten postoperatif 1,6'ya gerilemiş olup hastaların %85,7'si cerrahiden memnun kalmıştır.
tez.ozet: Giriş ve Amaç: Akalazya hastalığı alt özofagus sfinkterinin (AÖS) gevşeyememesi ve özofagusta peristaltizmin kaybı ile seyreden nadir bir motilite bozukluğudur. Bu çalışma laparoskopik Heller miyotomi ve Dor fundoplikasyonu (LHMD) uygulanan tip II akalazyalı hastalarda cerrahi başarıyı değerlendirmeyi ve semptom kontrolü ile yaşam kalitesini etkileyen faktörleri belirlemeyi amaçlamaktadır. Gereç ve Yöntem: 2019–2025 yılları arasında LHMD uygulanan 70 hasta retrospektif olarak incelenmiş, eksiksiz takibi bulunan 56 tip II akalazya hastası analize dahil edilmiştir. Demografik özellikler, preoperatif semptom süresi, uygulanan ek işlemler, intraoperatif bulgular ve postoperatif takip verileri değerlendirilmiştir. Cerrahi etkinlik, preoperatif ve postoperatif Eckardt skorlarındaki (ES) değişim ile nükssüz izlem süresi (RFI) üzerinden analiz edilmiştir. Bulgular: Hastaların yaş ortalaması 45,6 yıl olup %55,4'ü erkekti. Tüm hastalarda disfaji ve kilo kaybı mevcutken regürjitasyon %73,2, göğüs ağrısı %64,3 oranında izlendi. Ortalama operasyon süresi 150,6 dakika, median miyotomi uzunluğu 10 cm idi. İntraoperatif komplikasyon oranı %3,6 olarak saptandı. Median 22,9 aylık takipte nüks oranı %12,5, RFI median 19,2 ay bulundu. Toplam ES preoperatif 7,5'ten postoperatif 1,6'ya gerileyerek anlamlı iyileşme sağlandı. Hastaların %85,7'si cerrahiden memnun olduğunu bildirdi. Sonuç: LHMD tip II akalazya hastalarında yüksek semptomatik iyileşme, düşük komplikasyon oranı ve tatmin edici yaşam kalitesi artışı sağlamaktadır. Demografik değişkenler cerrahi başarıyı öngörmemekte; ES'deki belirgin düşüş cerrahi etkinliğin en güçlü göstergesi olarak öne çıkmaktadır.

makaleler.baslik: National Cross-Sectional Survey of Surgical Education Fellowships in the US.
makaleler.baslik_tr: ABD Cerrahi Eğitim Burslarının Ulusal Yapısı ve Kaynakları
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 28 cerrahi eğitim bursundan 19'unun katıldığı ulusal çaplı bir kesitsel ankette, programların %84'ünde eğitim, %89'unda simülasyon koordinasyonu zorunlu bulunmuştur. Bölüm bazlı Education PhD desteği %53, ücretsiz istatistikçi erişimi ise %63 oranında bildirilmiştir.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Surgical education fellowships prepare future surgeon-educators, yet national data describing training requirements and institutional support are limited. We characterized fellowship structure, educational responsibilities, and resources to inform program development and prospective fellows.
STUDY DESIGN: A national cross-sectional survey of accredited and non-accredited U.S. surgical education fellowships was conducted from April to December 2024. Representatives submitted collaborative program-level responses addressing structure, professional development, teaching, simulation, research infrastructure, and mentorship. Data were analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: Nineteen of 28 identified fellowships responded (68%), including 15 accredited and 4 non-accredited programs. Teaching was required by 16 programs (84%), simulation coordination and instruction by 17 (89%), and curriculum development by 15 (79%). However, only 10 programs (53%) reported departmental Education PhD support, and 12 (63%) provided access to statisticians at no cost. Sixteen programs (84%) offered fully funded fellowship positions. Three programs (16%) required completion of an advanced degree during the fellowship. Eight programs (42%) reserved positions for internal candidates. National conference attendance was required by 16 programs (84%). Fourteen programs (74%) had a single fellowship director; among directors with available data (n=21), median dedicated full-time equivalent was 0.2 (IQR 0,1).
CONCLUSIONS: U.S. surgical education fellowships share substantial teaching and simulation responsibilities but differ in institutional resources, professional development opportunities, and leadership support. These national descriptive findings provide improved transparency for prospective applicants, inform future fellowship development and resource allocation, and can guide research on graduate outcomes and accreditation. Longitudinal research is needed to determine how program characteristics and accreditation relate to graduate outcomes.

makaleler.baslik: ROBECS one: feasibility study of a structured robotic curriculum and a proficiency-based framework.
makaleler.baslik_tr: ROBECS One: Yapılandırılmış Robotik Müfredat ve Simülasyon Çalışması
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 6 kıdemli ve 15 asistanın katıldığı prospektif pilot çalışmada, 2 haftalık yapılandırılmış robotik simülasyon müfredatı başarıyla uygulanmıştır. Eğitim programı, temel ve teknik becerileri hedefleyen 6 ardışık modüle ayrılmıştır.
makaleler.ozet: Robotic surgery is increasingly integrated into surgical practice, yet structured, benchmark-driven simulation training remains limited for general surgery trainees. Proficiency-based progression (PBP) offers a practical, specialty-tested approach for structuring robotic surgical training around demonstrated performance rather than case numbers, but standardized PBP curricula for general surgery robotic training remain underdeveloped. This study aimed to test the feasibility of a structured, simulation-based robotic training and, building on this, to develop a preliminary proficiency-based approach whose benchmarks can be formally evaluated in future studies. We conducted a prospective, single-center pilot feasibility study of a structured robotic simulation curriculum over two weeks, combining virtual reality simulation and dry-lab training on the da Vinci Xi system (Intuitive Surgical, Sunnyvale, CA, USA). Advanced and novice robotic surgeons completed stepwise training sessions targeting core robotic skills and procedural tasks. Feasibility was defined by successful implementation within the timeframe, completion of sessions, and participant acceptance, assessed informally; the curriculum was subsequently structured into skill modules with proposed proficiency benchmarks. The curriculum was successfully implemented within the planned two-week timeframe, with six advanced and fifteen novice robotic surgeons participating. The curriculum was structured into six sequential modules, representing key technical and non-technical skills in robotic surgical practice, each with proposed proficiency benchmarks. This pilot study demonstrates the feasibility of a structured robotic simulation curriculum in general surgery. The proposed benchmark-driven structure may inform the development of standardized robotic simulation curricula for general surgery training programs, pending further validation against clinical performance.

makaleler.baslik: Gathering Response Process Validity Evidence for an Ultrasound-guided Thoracentesis Phantom Using Eye-tracking Metrics.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Ultrason Eşliğinde Torasentez Fantomu İçin Göz İzleme Metrikleri
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 13 deneyimli klinisyenin katıldığı çalışmada, göz izleme (ET) kullanılarak simüle edilmiş torasentez sırasında bilişsel iş yükü değerlendirilmiştir. Monitor üzerinde yapılan fiksasyonlar fantoma kıyasla anlamlı derecede yüksek bulunmuştur (91,6±12,4'e karşı 38,8±12,4; P<0,001).
makaleler.ozet:
INTRODUCTION: Simulation-based education is essential for developing procedural competence in ultrasound-guided thoracentesis (USGT). However, few USGT phantoms integrate objective metrics to assess cognitive workload. This study used eye tracking (ET) to quantify cognitive demand and establish preliminary validity evidence for a novel, anatomically variable USGT phantom.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Thirteen experienced clinicians performed simulated USGT on a modular phantom divided into 4 quadrants of increasing difficulty. Eye-tracking glasses recorded gaze behaviour across 2 areas of interest: the ultrasound monitor and the phantom. Cognitive workload was assessed through fixation and revisitation counts. Postsimulation, participants completed a Likert-scale questionnaire and provided qualitative feedback.
RESULTS: The monitor elicited significantly more fixations than the phantom [[91.6 ± 12.4 vs. 38.8 ± 12.4; F(1,87.1) = 20.26, P < 0.001], particularly in the most complex quadrant (Q3). Revisitation counts trended higher on the monitor but were not statistically significant overall (P = 0.08); however, Q3 showed significantly more revisitations than Q4 (P = 0.01). Q3 also required the most puncture attempts (2.31 ± 0.40; P = 0.001), aligning with increased cognitive workload. Realism and educational usefulness received high ratings (24/30 and 14.1/15, respectively). Thematic analysis highlighted anatomic fidelity, graduated difficulty, and integration of image acquisition with needle guidance as key strengths. ET revealed quadrant-specific variations in cognitive workload, demonstrating the phantom's structural design potential for progressive, scaffolded training. Fixation and revisitation metrics provided response process validity evidence, linking gaze behaviour to task complexity. Expert feedback confirmed the phantom's realism and educational value, reinforcing its feasibility as a platform for structured, just-in-time training.
CONCLUSION: ET offers a powerful lens to evaluate cognitive demands in procedural simulation. This study demonstrates how gaze metrics can inform phantom design and assessment, enhancing the fidelity and effectiveness of USGT training.
makaleler.dergi_tam: Simulation in healthcare : journal of the Society for Simulation in Healthcare

makaleler.baslik: Assessment of Technical Aptitude in Surgical Residency Applicants: A Scoping Review of the Literature.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Cerrahi Asistanlık Başvurularında Teknik Yeteneğin Değerlendirilmesi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Çeşitli cerrahi branşlardan 1301 başvuru sahibini içeren 21 çalışmanın incelendiği derlemede, teknik beceri değerlendirmelerinin uygulanabilir olduğu ancak psikometrik güç ve öngörüsel geçerliliğin sınırlı kaldığı gösterilmiştir.
makaleler.ozet:
OBJECTIVE: Surgical residency selection relies on traditional metrics that primarily assess cognitive performance and nontechnical attributes, offering limited insight into applicants' technical aptitude. In procedural specialties, early technical skill may influence operative performance and learning trajectories. Various psychomotor and simulation-based assessments have been proposed to evaluate technical ability in applicants, but their use is heterogeneous, and their value remains unclear. This scoping review aims to characterize technical aptitude assessments used in surgical residency applicants and evaluate available validity evidence, with emphasis on predictive utility.
METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, EMBASE, and Scopus (January 1947-March 11, 2026) identified studies evaluating performance-based technical assessments in surgical residency applicants. Studies were screened using predefined inclusion criteria. Data were extracted on study and assessment characteristics, outcome reporting, feasibility, and validity evidence using Messick's framework. Assessments were categorized by domain (manual dexterity, procedural skill, visuospatial ability) and modality (physical model, physical simulation, computer-based, robotic, paper-based). A narrative synthesis was performed.
RESULTS: Twenty-one studies involving 1301 applicants across multiple surgical specialties were included. Most assessments evaluated procedural skill using physical simulation administered during interview day. Outcome reporting was largely nondecomposed, and only a minority of studies included nontechnical outcomes. Evidence was most robust for response process and weakest for internal structure. Relations to other variables demonstrated the greatest variability, with only a small subset of studies showing strong predictive evidence, often using composite outcome scores as their predictor. Technical performance was frequently uncorrelated with traditional academic metrics. Feasibility was generally favorable, with low per-applicant costs.
CONCLUSIONS: Technical aptitude assessments in surgical residency applicants are feasible and capture constructs distinct from traditional academic metrics; however, their psychometric rigor and predictive validity remain limited and inconsistent. Standardization of assessment design and more rigorous investigation are needed before widespread adoption in residency selection.

makaleler.baslik: Evaluating the Feedback Quality of General Surgery Residents for Open Inguinal Hernia Repair.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Herni Onarımı Geri Bildirimlerinde İnsan ve Yapay Zekâ Değerlendirmesi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 1270 geri bildirim yorumunun incelendiği çalışmada, yapay zekâ modeli insan değerlendiricilere kıyasla anlamlı derecede yüksek bileşik skorlar üretmiştir (p<0,001). PGY1 düzeyindeki asistanlar en yüksek kaliteli geri bildirimi alırken, PGY4 ve PGY5 asistanlarına daha düşük skorlar verilmiştir.
makaleler.ozet:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to 1) compare human rater and machine learning (ML) evaluations of feedback quality and 2) examine differences in how feedback quality varies by PGY level for human rater and ML approaches.
DESIGN: Dictated feedback comments from one surgical procedure (open inguinal hernia repair) across all surgical training years were evaluated using 2 approaches: (1) human raters using the Quality of Assessment of Learning (QuAL) Score rubric and (2) a ML model trained using the QuAL Score rubric. Human-based and ML scores were compared using a Mann-Whitney U test. For each scoring approach, a Kruskal Wallis test was performed to identify differences in composite scores across each postgraduate year (PGY) level. Dunn's posthoc test was used to determine which combination of training years had significantly different scores.
SETTING: Surgical environments that use the Society for Improving Medical Professional Learning (SIMPL) application.
PARTICIPANTS: General surgery residents in the United States between 2015 and 2023 who received dictated feedback comments from the SIMPL application.
RESULTS: A total of 1270 dictated feedback comments across all PGYs were analyzed. For composite scores, the ML model produced significantly higher scores compared to the human rater (p < 0.001). This remained true for both the evidence (p < 0.001) and connection (p < 0.001) subscores. There was no significant difference for suggestion subscores (p = 0.843). Significant differences were found for both the human rater (p < 0.01) and the ML model (p < 0.01) when evaluating differences across PGYs. Specifically, posthoc differences were found between PGY1 and PGY2, PGY1 and PGY4, and between PGY1 and PGY5, with higher quality scores given to the PGY1s and lower quality scores given to the PGY 4s and 5s.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite using the same QuAL scoring rubric, our study revealed some significant differences in evaluation scores produced by human raters and the ML model. The ML model produced higher feedback composite scores, driven mostly by the evidence and connection subscore domains. Differences were also found in evaluations of feedback quality across the PGY levels, with PGY1 residents receiving the highest quality feedback. Although these findings contribute initial validity evidence to guide how ML models could and should be used to evaluate feedback quality, more testing and research is warranted before these models can be confidently deployed.

makaleler.baslik: External Validation of a Machine Learning Model for Delirium Risk.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Deliryum Risk Modeli İçin Harici Doğrulama Çalışması
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Yoğun bakım dışı yatan hastalarda yapay zekâ tabanlı deliryum risk stratifikasyon modelinin harici doğrulaması yapılmıştır. 33.095 hastanın dahil olduğu çalışmada model AUROC değeri 0,91 ile 0,94 arasında bulunmuş, model sonrası aylık deliryum saptama oranı %9,23'ten %19,59'a yükselmiştir.
makaleler.ozet:
IMPORTANCE: Although external validation of machine learning (ML)-based delirium risk models is a key stage in the model development pipeline, few published reports exist. Moreover, ML-based delirium risk models commonly degrade in performance during external validation.
OBJECTIVE: To examine the performance of a fusion multimodal with natural language processing (NLP) delirium risk stratification model in live clinical practice with cross-hospital external validation.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This quality improvement study evaluated live clinical deployment of the model among patients 60 years or older who were admitted to non-intensive care units at Mount Sinai Hospital (MSH), with external validation performed at Mount Sinai Morningside Hospital (MSM), from December 1, 2024, to December 31, 2025.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes were performance of the risk stratification model, assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), and monthly delirium detection rates. A 2 × 2 confusion matrix was created, and the 4 cells were used to calculate model performance metrics and compare associated diagnostic yield between premodel deployment and active model deployment periods.
RESULTS: The overall sample included 33 095 admissions to non-intensive care units at MSM and MSH (mean [SD] age, 74.86 (9.22) years; 15 601 women [47.1%], 17 271 men [52.2%]). A total of 9020 MSM inpatient admissions were assigned a delirium risk score by the risk stratification model during live clinical operations and were compared to 21 186 MSH inpatient admissions that were assigned a risk score by the same model. Age at admission significantly differed between patients at MSM and MSH (MSM: median [IQR] age, 75.79 [68.25-83.88] years vs MSH: 72.62 [66.64-79.65] years; P < .001). Patients from MSM and MSH also significantly differed by sex, race and ethnicity, surgical vs medical primary diagnosis, length of stay, and dementia prevalence rate. Among 11 909 MSM patients, patients in the pre-ML cohort (median [IQR] age, 78.00 [71.00-85.00] years) were significantly older than those in the post-ML cohort (median [IQR] age, 75.79 [68.25-83.88] years) (P < .001). The AUROC of the model was 0.91 (95% CI, 0.90-0.92) for MSM and 0.94 (95% CI, 0.93-0.94) for MSH. The positive predictive value of the model was 25.9% for MSM and 19.4% for MSH. For MSM, the mean monthly delirium detection rate significantly increased from 9.23% (95% CI, 8.07%-10.38%) to 19.59% (95% CI, 17.32%-21.85%) after model deployment (P < .001).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this quality improvement study, an ML-based delirium risk stratification model maintained acceptable discriminative performance during external deployment without retraining and was similar to its performance at the development site without retraining. Model deployment was also associated with increased diagnostic yield but a high false positive rate. These findings provide further evidence of the potential generalizability of the model.

makaleler.baslik: Quantitative CT definition of solid components in pulmonary ground-glass nodules: a pixel-level annotation-based development and internal validation study.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Pulmoner Nodüllerde Katı Komponentlerin Kantitatif CT Tanımı
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Cerrahi olarak rezeke edilen 170 evre I akciğer adenokarsinomu olgusunda katı komponentin değerlendirilmesi için lezyona adaptif kantitatif CT yöntemleri geliştirilmiştir. GGO ortalama artı oran yöntemi AUC 0,848, sensitivite 0,732 ve spesifisite 0,815 ile en iyi performansı göstermiştir.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Solid-component assessment in pulmonary ground-glass nodules (GGNs) remains subjective, and no universally accepted computed tomography (CT) attenuation threshold exists. Fixed cutoffs may not account for inter-lesion variation in baseline ground-glass opacity (GGO) attenuation. We aimed to develop and internally validate lesion-adaptive quantitative CT definitions of the solid component using three-dimensional pixel-level expert annotations as the imaging reference standard.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center methodological study included 170 unique patients with 170 surgically resected stage I lung adenocarcinoma-spectrum GGNs from March 2015 through July 2018 and each patient contributed one target lesion. All examinations were acquired on the same 256-row CT scanner, and venous-phase 1-mm images reconstructed with medium-strength deep learning image reconstruction were used for analysis. Each lesion was independently annotated by at least two experienced thoracic surgeons, with Dice-based adjudication and senior review. Patients were randomly allocated to training (n=120) and internal validation (n=50) cohorts. Nine prespecified study methods and three literature-based fixed thresholds were evaluated at pixel and lesion levels.
RESULTS: The training and validation cohorts had median lesion sizes of 1.2 and 1.3 cm and median annotated solid-component proportions of 0.324 and 0.319, respectively. The GGO mean plus ratio method achieved the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve [AUC, 0.848; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.841-0.856], with sensitivity of 0.732, specificity of 0.815, and F1/Dice of 0.760. The GGO mean plus difference method yielded the highest lesion-level coefficient of determination (R2, 0.744; 95% CI: 0.499-0.889), whereas the ratio method yielded the lowest root mean square error (RMSE, 0.105) and mean absolute error (MAE, 0.088). Pairwise DeLong testing showed no statistically significant AUC difference among the three top-performing GGO-referenced methods.
CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center internal validation study, lesion-adaptive GGO-referenced methods showed more favorable overall pixel-level discrimination and lesion-level agreement than universal fixed thresholds or lesion-summary estimators. These rules should be considered developmental quantitative methods and require multicenter external validation across CT platforms and reconstruction protocols before routine clinical use.

makaleler.baslik: Active learning for efficient annotation of surgical videos with weak supervision.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Cerrahi Videoların Zayıf Denetimli Etiketlenmesi İçin Aktif Öğrenme
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Laparoskopik videoların zamansal-uzamsal etiketleme eforunu azaltmak amacıyla aktif öğrenme ve ikili kayıp optimizasyonunu birleştiren bir insan-döngü çerçevesi önerilmiştir. Geliştirilen bu yöntem, tam manuel etiketlemeye kıyasla cerrahi video etiketleme çabasını yaklaşık %50 oranında azaltmıştır.
makaleler.ozet:
PURPOSE: Precise spatial-temporal annotation of laparoscopic videos is time-consuming and requires expert knowledge. We propose a human-in-the-loop knowledge acquisition framework that combines active learning with dual-loss optimization to significantly reduce the annotation effort needed for automatic localization and segmentation of objects in the surgical field.
METHODS: Our method employs a foundation model to generate temporally consistent class activation maps (CAMs) from video using two complementary training objectives: a weak supervision loss on video-level tool presence labels for weakly annotated data, and an image-level mask loss on human-corrected annotations obtained through active learning. Rather than requiring dense pixel-level annotation upfront, our pipeline iteratively proposes pseudo-masks that guide the expert annotator to refine the knowledge previously captured by the model.
RESULTS: We demonstrate that our framework reduces the effort of surgical video annotation by approximately 50% by the end of training in comparison to fully manual annotation.
CONCLUSION: Through eliminating the need for large, fully annotated datasets from the start, this framework enables scalability to the development of surgical tool segmentation models. This iterative human-in-the-loop refinement supports efficient knowledge acquisition with minimal expert input, providing a practical and deployable strategy for expanding tool segmentation to larger, more diverse datasets and real-world clinical settings. Code shared at: https://github.com/PCASOlab/AL-WSL .

makaleler.baslik: Artificial intelligence for vascular minimally invasive surgery: techniques, clinical integration, and challenges.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Vasküler Minimal İnvaziv Cerrahide Yapay Zeka Uygulamaları
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Analiz edilen 30 birincil çalışmada machine learning risk stratifikasyonunu desteklemiş, deep learning görüntüleme uygulamaları sağlamış, natural language processing bilgi çıkarımını kolaylaştırmıştır. Klinik adaptasyon için daha güçlü validasyon gereklidir.
makaleler.ozet:
INTRODUCTION: Minimally invasive surgery (MIS), including endovascular and robot-assisted procedures, is widely used for vascular pathologies but remains limited by technical complexity, cognitive workload, and postoperative complications. Artificial Intelligence (AI) may help address these challenges through predictive analysis, decision support, image analysis, and automation.
METHODS: A structured Google Scholar search was conducted from February 21, 2025, to January 1, 2026, and updated through September 2026. Peer-reviewed studies applying AI to vascular MIS were included, with additional targeted searches addressing clinical translation, deployment, regulation, and ethical considerations.
RESULTS: Thirty primary studies were analyzed, including eight on machine learning, nine on deep learning, four on natural language processing, and nine on robotics or reinforcement learning. Machine learning supported risk stratification and outcome prediction, deep learning enabled imaging and segmentation applications, natural language processing facilitated clinical information extraction, and robotic systems supported navigation and procedural assistance.
DISCUSSION: AI demonstrates substantial potential across the vascular MIS pathway, but broader clinical adoption requires stronger validation, prospective multicenter studies, standardized reporting, health-economic evaluation, and careful consideration of regulatory, liability, and accessibility challenges.

makaleler.baslik: AI-accelerated compressed sensing and deep learning reconstruction for colon MRI: prospective validation of image quality and preliminary assessment of staging accuracy versus contrast-enhanced CT.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Kolon MR İçin Yapay Zeka Destekli Görüntüleme ve Evreleme Doğrulaması
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 132 hastada yapılan tek merkezli çalışmada, AI destekli MR protokolu CECT'ye kıyasla daha yüksek görüntü kalitesi skoru (4'e karşı 3) ve T-evreleme doğruluğu (%78,8'e karşı %30,3) sağlamıştır.
makaleler.ozet:
OBJECTIVES: To prospectively validate an AI-accelerated MRI protocol combining L₁-regularized compressed sensing and deep learning reconstruction for colon cancer staging, compared with contrast-enhanced CT (CECT).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center study (August 2022-April 2024) enrolled 132 patients with pathologically confirmed colon cancer who underwent both 3.0-T non-contrast MRI and CECT within 1 week. Patients unable to complete an MRI were excluded. MRI sequences included T1- and T2-weighted imaging and diffusion-weighted imaging. Image quality was assessed using a 4-point Likert scale, alongside quantitative analysis of contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) and edge rise distance (ERD). Surgical pathology correlation was available for 33 cases. Five radiologists independently reviewed the images.
RESULTS: Among 153 matched examination pairs from 132 patients (mean age, 58 ± 11 years), AI-MRI outperformed CECT in both qualitative and quantitative measures. MRI yielded higher image quality scores (4 [IQR 3-4] vs. 3 [IQR 3-3]), improved CNR (5.5 [IQR 4.2-7.0] vs. 1.3 [IQR 0.7-2.2]), and reduced ERD (1.6 mm [IQR 1.2-2.8] vs. 3.7 mm [IQR 2.8-5.0]). MRI provided superior peritoneal sharpness (75.8%) and colonic wall visualization (100%), and superior or equivalent tumor conspicuity (92.2%) and nodal assessment (86.9%), whereas CECT demonstrated better artifact control (45.1%). In preliminary analyses, MRI achieved higher T-staging accuracy (78.8% vs. 30.3%) and N-staging specificity (93.3% vs. 13.3%).
CONCLUSION: The AI-accelerated MRI protocol significantly outperformed CECT in image quality and preliminary staging accuracy for colon cancer evaluation while eliminating radiation exposure.
KEY POINTS: Question Can an AI-accelerated MRI protocol provide superior image quality and staging performance compared with contrast-enhanced CT, which has limited diagnostic accuracy for colon cancer staging? Findings AI-accelerated MRI using L₁-regularized compressed sensing and deep learning reconstruction achieved superior image quality and higher preliminary staging accuracy than contrast-enhanced CT. Critical Relevance Statement AI-accelerated MRI improves image quality and staging confidence without radiation exposure, supporting its potential to enhance preoperative assessment and clinical decision-making in colon cancer.

tez.baslik: 18F-FDG PET ve PET/CT görüntülemelerinde taşlı yüzük hücreli mide kanserlerinin yapay zeka destekli tanısı
tez.baslik_tr: Mide Kanserlerinde Yapay Zeka Destekli PET/CT Tanısı
tez.kisa_ozet: 171 hastanın 1189 PET görüntüsü ile yapılan retrospektif çalışmada, geliştirilen derin öğrenme modelinin genel doğruluk oranı %84,97 olarak hesaplanmıştır. Adenokarsinom grubunda duyarlılık %92,75 iken, taşlı yüzük hücreli karsinom grubunda duyarlılık %62,22 olarak belirlenmiştir.
tez.ozet: Amaç: Histopatolojik açıdan taşlı yüzük hücreli mide kanseri (SRCC), adenokarsinomdan farklılık göstermesine rağmen, çoğu zaman 18F-FDG PET ve PET/BT görüntülemelerinde, düşük FDG tutulumu nedeniyle tanı sürecinde gözden kaçabilmektedir. Bu durum, hastalığın tespit edilmesinin ve dolayısıyla tedavi planlamasınn gecikmesine neden olabilmektedir. Bu çalışmadaki temel amaç, taşlı yüzük hücreli mide karsinomu alt tipinin tanısını kolaylaştırmak için yalnızca 18F-FDG PET görüntülerine dayalı geliştirilen yapay zeka tabanlı bir modelin tanı doğruluğunu, duyarlılığını ve özgüllük performansını değerlendirmektir. Geliştirilen derin öğrenme algoritmasının, geleneksel tanı ve evreleme yaklaşımlarına yardımcı olacak şekilde klinik karar süreçlerine katkıda bulunmasına, tanının erken konulmasına olanak tanımasına ve tedavi stratejilerinin optimize edilmesine destek olması hedeflenmektedir. Gereç ve Yöntem: Bu retrospektif çalışmaya, İstanbul Eğitim ve Araştırma Hastanesi'nde tanı almış toplam 171 hasta dahil edilmiştir. Adeno (adenokanser) grubunda 63, SRCC (taşlı yüzük hücreli karsinom) grubunda 53 ve kontrol grubunda 55 hasta yer almıştır. Bu hastalara ait toplam 1189 adet PET görüntüsü kesidi, mide bölgesini içerecek şekilde kırpılarak (crop) analiz edilmiştir. Görüntüler eğitim (%70), doğrulama (%15) ve test (%15) setlerine ayrılmıştır. Derin öğrenme modelinde DenseNet121, EfficientNet-B4 ve ConvNeXt-Tiny mimarilerinden oluşan bir ensemble yapı kullanılmış; sınıf dengesizliğini azaltmak için SRCC grubuna yönelik focal loss uygulanmıştır. Model, Google Colab Pro+ platformunda, NVIDIA A100 GPU üzerinde eğitilmiştir. Performans ölçütü olarak doğruluk, duyarlılık, özgüllük, pozitif ve negatif prediktif değerler, F1 skoru, ROC-AUC ve Ki-kare testi kullanılmıştır. Bulgular: Test verileri üzerinde modelin genel doğruluk oranı %84,97 olarak hesaplanmıştır. Adeno (adenokarsinom) grubunda duyarlılık %92,75, pozitif prediktif değer %87,67 ve F1 skoru 0.9014 olarak bulunurken; SRCC (taşlı yüzük hücreli karsinom) grubunda duyarlılık %62,22, pozitif prediktif değer %75,68 ve F1 skoru 0.6829 olarak belirlenmiştir. ROC eğrisi altında kalan alan (AUC) Adeno ve kontrol gruplarında sırasıyla 0.94 ve 0.96 iken, SRCC için 0.78 olarak tespit edilmiştir. Ki-kare testi sonucunda sınıflar arasında anlamlı bir fark olduğu gösterilmiştir (p<0.00001). Cramér's V değeri 0.649 olup, modelin tahminleriyle gerçek sınıf dağılımı arasında güçlü bir ilişki saptanmıştır. Sonuç: Geliştirilen derin öğrenme modeli, yalnızca PET görüntülerine dayanarak mide kanserinin histolojik alt tipleri olan adenokarsinomu ve taşlı yüzük hücreli karsinomu (SRCC) yüksek doğrulukla ayırt edebilmiştir. Özellikle Adeno ve kontrol gruplarında başarılı sonuçlar elde edilmiş; SRCC sınıfında ise histolojik heterojeniteye bağlı olarak modelin performansının görece sınırlı kaldığı düşünülmektedir. Bu çalışma, yapay zekâ destekli görüntü analiziyle mide kanseri alt tiplerinin non-invaziv ayrımının mümkün olabileceğini göstermektedir. Ayrıca, yapay zekâ tabanlı PET analizleri, yalnızca tanısal doğruluk açısından değil; aynı zamanda gereksiz biyopsi, ileri tetkik ve tedavi maliyetlerini azaltarak sağlık sistemlerinde maliyet-etkinliği artırma potansiyeli taşımaktadır. Bu yaklaşım, yüksek riskli bireylerin daha doğru seçilmesine ve tarama sürecinin optimize edilmesine katkı sunabilir. Gelecekte daha geniş örneklem büyüklüğüne sahip, çok merkezli ve segmentasyonla zenginleştirilmiş veri setleriyle yürütülecek çalışmalar, modelin klinik pratikte uygulanabilirliğini daha somut biçimde ortaya koyabilir ve yapay zekâ tabanlı tanı sistemlerinin rutin kullanımına yönelik önemli bir temel oluşturabilir. Anahtar Kelimeler: Mide kanseri, yapay zekâ, PET görüntüleme, adenokarsinom, taşlı yüzük hücreli karsinom, derin öğrenme, CNN

makaleler.baslik: Chronic corticosteroid therapy impairs postoperative outcomes of pancreatic surgery: International multicenter retrospective study.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Kronik Kortikosteroid Tedavisinin Pankreas Cerrahisi Sonuçlarına Etkisi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 2564 hastanın dahil olduğu uluslararası çalışmada, kronik kortikosteroid tedavisi majör morbiditeyi artırmış (%59,2'ye karşı %30,6; p<0,001) ve enfeksiyon komplikasyonları ile ilişkili bulunmuştur (OR 4,66).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Patients receiving chronic corticosteroid therapy often have complex conditions and may face an increased risk of adverse postoperative outcomes. In pancreatic surgery, pancreas-specific and infectious complications significantly affect recovery, but evidence on the impact of chronic corticosteroid therapy remains limited.
METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included patients undergoing pancreatic resection between 2012 and 2025. Chronic corticosteroid therapy was defined as systemic corticosteroids at a prednisone-equivalent dose ≥5 mg/d for ≥4 consecutive weeks before surgery. Propensity score matching was performed within each center in a 1:3 ratio using age, sex, body mass index, Charlson Comorbidity Index, and type of pancreatic resection. The primary outcome was major morbidity, defined as Clavien-Dindo ≥IIIa.
RESULTS: Of 2,564 patients, 52 received chronic corticosteroid therapy. After matching, 49 patients receiving chronic corticosteroid therapy were compared with 147 patients not receiving chronic corticosteroid therapy. Chronic corticosteroid therapy was associated with worse postoperative outcomes, including major morbidity (59.2% vs 30.6%; P < .001), Comprehensive Complication Index (34.6 vs 20.9; P < .001), longer postoperative hospital stays (15 vs 10 days; P = .007), 30-day readmission (29.5% vs 15.8%; P = .049), and 90-day mortality (10.2% vs 2.0%; P = .025). Infectious complications were more frequent, especially deep incisional surgical site infection/organ-space infection, sepsis, and pneumonia (all P < .05). In matched conditional logistic regression, chronic corticosteroid therapy remained associated with major morbidity (odds ratio, 3.20; 95% confidence interval, 1.63-6.28) and infectious complications (odds ratio, 4.66; 95% confidence interval, 2.31-9.40).
CONCLUSION: Chronic corticosteroid therapy identifies a higher-risk subgroup undergoing pancreatic resection, supporting its inclusion in perioperative risk stratification and multidisciplinary planning.

gundem.baslik: The Japanese Hernia Society (JHS) Guidelines for Adult Groin Hernia Management 2024.
gundem.baslik_tr: JHS 2024 Erişkin Kasık Hernisi Yönetimi Kılavuzu
gundem.kisa_ozet: Japon Herni Derneği (JHS) 2024 kılavuzu; tanı, sınıflandırma, cerrahi endikasyonlar, teknikler, mesh tespiti, anestezi, kronik ağrı ve acil herni yönetimi konularında öneriler sunar. Deneyimli cerrahlar tarafından seçilmiş hastalarda laparoskopik onarım tercih edilirken, açık anterior mesh onarımı uygun durumlarda geçerliliğini korur.
gundem.ozet: Groin hernia is a common surgical condition. The Japanese Hernia Society (JHS) Guidelines for Groin Hernia Management 2024 were developed to reflect both international evidence and the realities of clinical practice in Japan. This article is an authorized English translation of a summary of the adult section of the JHS Guidelines for Groin Hernia Management 2024, presenting key clinical questions, recommendations, and concise explanations for an international readership. It covers diagnosis, classification, surgical indications, operative approaches, mesh and fixation, anesthesia, chronic postoperative inguinal pain, recurrent and emergency hernia, training, cost-effectiveness, and registry-based outcome assessment; relevant differences from the international HerniaSurge guidelines are discussed. Laparoscopic repair is favored in selected patients when performed by experienced surgeons, particularly for pain reduction and early recovery, whereas open anterior mesh repair remains appropriate when general anesthesia or laparoscopy is unsuitable. For femoral hernia, chronic pain management, recurrent hernia, and incarcerated or strangulated hernia, evidence remains limited, leading to cautious or conditional recommendations.

gundem.baslik: Robotic versus laparoscopic gastrectomy for gastric cancer: 5-year long-term results from a randomized controlled trial.
gundem.baslik_tr: Mide Kanserinde Robotik ve Laparoskopik Gastrektomi: 5 Yıllık Sonuçlar
gundem.kisa_ozet: Resektabl mide kanserli 241 hastayı içeren bir faz III RCT'de, laparoskopik ve robotik gastrektomi arasında 5 yıllık relapse-free survival (%69'a karşı %75) ve overall survival (%71'e karşı %79) açısından anlamlı fark saptanmamıştır. Erkek alt grubunda robotik grupta overall survival daha iyi bulunmuştur (HR 0,48; %95 CI 0,25-0,95).
gundem.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Despite increasing global adoption of robotic approaches, the comparative effectiveness of robotic gastrectomy versus laparoscopic gastrectomy for gastric cancer is uncertain, particularly regarding long-term oncologic outcomes.
METHODS: This phase III randomized controlled trial (RCT) enrolled 241 patients with resectable gastric cancer (clinical stages I-III) between April 1, 2018, and October 31, 2020. Patients were randomly assigned to undergo either robotic gastrectomy or laparoscopic gastrectomy. The primary endpoint was postoperative intra-abdominal infectious complications (previously reported). Secondary endpoints included long-term oncologic outcomes, specifically relapse-free survival, overall survival and patterns of recurrence.
RESULTS: This study enrolled 241 patients, with 236 patients in the modified intention-to-treat population. The 5-year relapse-free survival in the modified intention-to-treat population did not significantly differ between the laparoscopic gastrectomy and robotic gastrectomy groups (69% vs. 75%). Similarly, overall survival was not significantly different between the groups (71% vs. 79%). The 5-year cumulative incidence of primary disease-specific death was comparable between the groups (16.1% vs. 11.6%). Patterns of recurrence did not differ between them. In subgroup analyses, the robotic gastrectomy group demonstrated significantly better overall survival than the laparoscopic gastrectomy group among male patients (HR, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.25-0.95). Among patients that underwent distal gastrectomy, the robotic gastrectomy group showed a significantly lower cumulative incidence of primary disease-specific death than the laparoscopic gastrectomy group (HR, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.07-0.81).
CONCLUSION: In this RCT, secondary endpoint analyses showed no statistically significant differences in 5-year relapse-free survival or overall survival between laparoscopic gastrectomy and robotic gastrectomy.

gundem.baslik: Effect of pancreatic neck transection site on postoperative complications after laparoscopic pancreaticoduodenectomy: a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
gundem.baslik_tr: Laparoskopik Pankreatikoduodenektomide Pankreas Boyun Kesi Yerinin Komplikasyonlara Etkisi
gundem.kisa_ozet: 141 hastanın dahil olduğu çok merkezli bu RCT'de, genişletilmiş pankreas boyun kesisi (EPNT) grubunda klinik olarak anlamlı postoperatif pankreatik fistül (CR-POPF) insidansı %10,9 iken, konvansiyonel kesi (CPNT) grubunda %26,0 saptanmıştır (RR=0,42; %95 CI 0,19-0,93; P=0,031). EPNT ayrıca enfeksiyöz komplikasyonları da anlamlı derecede azaltmıştır.
gundem.ozet:
AIM/BACKGROUND: Theoretical controversy persists regarding the optimal pancreatic neck transection site during laparoscopic pancreaticoduodenectomy (LPD). This study aimed to investigate the impact of pancreatic neck transection level on postoperative complications after LPD.
METHODS: This multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial was conducted at four high-volume pancreatic surgery centers in China. Patients scheduled for LPD were randomly assigned to undergo pancreatic neck transection at different sites. In the extended pancreatic neck transection (EPNT) group, transection was performed 5-10 mm lateral to the left margin of the superior mesenteric vein-portal vein (SMV-PV) axis. While in the conventional pancreatic neck transection (CPNT) group, transection was carried out anterior to the SMV-PV axis. The primary outcome measure was the incidence of clinically relevant postoperative pancreatic fistula (CR-POPF), and analyses were performed based on the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) analysis.
RESULTS: Among 152 eligible patients, 141 were randomized and included in the mITT analysis. Sixty four patients were allocated to the EPNT group and 77 to the CPNT group. The incidence of CR-POPF was 10.9% in the EPNT group versus 26.0% in the CPNT group (RR = 0.42, 95%CI 0.19-0.93, P = 0.031). Additionally, the EPNT group exhibited a significantly lower incidence of infectious complications compared with the CPNT group (10.9% vs. 26.0%, P = 0.031). No statistically significant intergroup differences were detected with respect to other perioperative complications (P > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Compared with CPNT, EPNT significantly reduces the incidences of CR-POPF and infectious complications following LPD without elevating the risk of other complications.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT05808894.

gundem.baslik: Efficacy and Safety of Prophylactic Defect Closure After Colorectal ESD: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis with GRADE Certainty Assessment.
gundem.baslik_tr: Kolorektal ESD Sonrası Profilaktik Defekt Kapatma
gundem.kisa_ozet: 5.830 prosedürü içeren 16 çalışmanın sistematik derleme ve meta-analizinde, kolorektal ESD sonrası profilaktik defekt kapatmanın gecikmiş kanama riskini azalttığı gösterildi (RR 0,42; %95 CI, 0,28-0,62; pooled oranlar %2,4'e karşı %6,9). Gecikmiş perforasyon veya hastane kalış süresinde fark görülmedi.
gundem.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Colorectal endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) leaves a large mucosal defect that predisposes patients to delayed adverse events, chiefly delayed bleeding. Prophylactic closure of the defect has been proposed to improve safety, but its overall efficacy remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis provides an updated synthesis of the safety and efficacy of prophylactic mucosal defect closure after colorectal ESD.
METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched from inception to June 2026, without language restrictions, for randomized controlled trials and comparative observational studies comparing prophylactic closure with no closure after colorectal ESD. The primary outcome was delayed bleeding; secondary outcomes were delayed perforation, post-ESD coagulation syndrome (PECS), and length of hospital stay. Pooled RRs and mean differences with 95% CIs were calculated using random-effects models, and the certainty of evidence was assessed with GRADE.
RESULTS: Sixteen studies comprising 5,830 procedures were included. Prophylactic closure was associated with a lower risk of delayed bleeding (RR 0.42; 95% CI, 0.28 to 0.62; I² = 63.9%), with pooled delayed bleeding rates of 2.4% with closure and 6.9% without closure. No difference was observed for delayed perforation (RR 0.89; 95% CI, 0.37 to 2.17), PECS (RR 1.12; 95% CI, 0.50 to 2.49), or length of hospital stay (mean difference 0.16 days; 95% CI, -0.61 to 0.93). Small-study effects were detected for delayed bleeding, and the certainty of evidence ranged from low to very low.
CONCLUSIONS: Prophylactic closure after colorectal ESD reduced delayed bleeding. No effect on delayed perforation, PECS, or length of hospital stay was shown, although these estimates were imprecise. Closure may be best reserved for patients at high risk of bleeding.

gundem.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Numerous 5-hydroxytryptamine 3 receptor antagonists are available to prevent postoperative nausea and vomiting after laparoscopic cholecystectomy, but relevant comparative data are limited.
AIMS: This study aimed to compare various 5-hydroxytryptamine 3 receptor antagonists in preventing postoperative nausea and vomiting after laparoscopic cholecystectomy via systematic review and network meta-analysis.
METHODS: This study followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses statement. We systematically searched for articles in PubMed, Cochrane, Embase, and WOS up to August 2025. The quality of included studies was assessed utilizing the National Institutes of Health Study Quality Assessment Tools. Network meta-analysis was performed to evaluate the effectiveness (risk ratio) of various 5-hydroxytryptamine 3 receptor antagonists, different doses, and usage time of various 5-hydroxytryptamine 3 receptor antagonists in postoperative nausea and vomiting prevention after laparoscopic cholecystectomy. To avoid anomalies in data analysis caused by the absence of postoperative nausea and vomiting, no postoperative nausea and vomiting was analyzed.
RESULTS: A total of 21 studies (n = 2,033 patients) were included. The results revealed that compared with placebo, ramosetron (risk ratio, 2.60) and palonosetron (risk ratio, 2.50) pronouncedly prevented postoperative nausea and vomiting; tropisetron (risk ratio, 0.23), ramosetron (risk ratio, 0.25), and palonosetron (risk ratio, 0.27) significantly prevented nausea; ramosetron (risk ratio, 0.10) markedly prevented vomiting. Ramosetron (risk ratio, 0.43) demonstrated greater efficacy than ondansetron in preventing retching. In subgroup analyses, ondansetron 8 mg outperformed ondansetron 4 mg in preventing nausea, vomiting, and retching. The administration of ondansetron, ramosetron, palonosetron, and granisetron at the end of the operation outperformed preoperative administration in postoperative nausea and vomiting.
CONCLUSION: Among the 5-hydroxytryptamine 3 receptor antagonists, palonosetron and ramosetron show better efficacy in preventing postoperative nausea and vomiting after laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Subgroup analyses show that 8 mg of ondansetron outperforms 4 mg of ondansetron. Administration of drugs at the end of the operation outperforms preoperative administration.
